There is a constructor Position(entry, exit, transactionModel, holdingModel). There is also Position() default empty. There is Position(TradeType, CostModel, CostModel). For exception scenarios we might need to mock Position to force getProfit to throw. But we can also use Mockito spy to stub getProfit to throw exceptions. Since hasProfit just calls getProfit().isPositive(), we can spy Position and stub getProfit to throw.

Thus we can create tests using Mockito to simulate exceptions.

Not sure. Could use DoubleNum.valueOf(Double.NaN). But getProfit may return NaN if price missing. To simulate, we can spy Position and stub getProfit to return NaN. Then hasProfit false.

Test short position scenarios: For short (SELL) entry, we need to create Position with entry SELL, exit BUY. Use Trade.sellAt for entry? So we need to construct Position(entrySellHigh, exitBuyLow). Check constructors.

Test open position scenarios: open position (no exit) has hasProfit false. Already covered.

Extreme profit values: Use huge numbers.

Exception scenarios: Use spy to throw NullPointerException, IllegalStateException, ArithmeticException, IllegalArgumentException.
